evals.prompt: I just wrote a new command handler for creating template items. Write tests for it.
evals.expected_output: Routes to context/write.md. Identifies the handler as application-layer logic needing unit tests. Follows TDD: generates a test list (happy path, validation failures, edge cases), names tests using the consuming project's documented naming pattern (mirroring the ecosystem's own idiom when undocumented), and places them in the project's documented co-located test location. Defers to the consuming project's documented framework and assertion conventions rather than assuming any specific stack.

evals.prompt: Where should I put integration tests for a new shared library?
evals.expected_output: Routes to context/organize.md. Evaluates whether the library has testable behavior (business logic, conditional branching) vs pure contracts. If testable: a dedicated test project is warranted; its placement turns on whether the integration tests are single-project (co-locate with the library) or cross-project (centralize under the integration-test root) — inspects or asks for the consuming project's documented naming and location convention to decide, rather than pre-committing to either branch. If contracts only: no dedicated test project needed, transitive coverage acceptable.

evals.name: does-not-skip-red-on-an-obvious-fix
evals.prompt: Write tests for this parser, but I already know the bug, so skip the failing test and just patch it.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to skip Red. Follows TDD: writes the failing test first, then the minimal fix, then retests. Does not patch production code before a failing test exists.
expectations: Writes or requires a failing test before changing production code
Does not skip the red step because the fix seems obvious
Names the consuming project's test location and naming pattern rather than inventing a stack

evals.name: round-trip-duration-format-routes-to-property-guidance
evals.prompt: Our config loader has format_duration, which turns a number of seconds into strings like '1h30m', and parse_duration, which reads them back. Add tests for both.
evals.expected_output: Routes to context/property.md because a formatter and its parser form a reverse pair. Writes a property whose oracle is the round trip: parsing the formatted string returns the original number of seconds for every generated non-negative duration. Also keeps a couple of literal examples such as 5400 seconds formatting as '1h30m'.
expectations: Reads context/property.md before writing the tests
Uses the round trip (parse of format equals the input) as the property's oracle
Does not build the expected string inside the test by repeating the formatter's arithmetic

evals.name: rejects-property-that-reimplements-algorithm
evals.prompt: Review my property test for split_bill(total_cents, people): for any total and head count it asserts the result equals [total_cents // people] * people. Is that a good property? Fix it.
evals.expected_output: Rejects the oracle: the expected side repeats the splitting arithmetic, so a mistake shared by test and code still passes (and here it also drops the remainder cents). Points to /testing:test-value for the rule that an expected value needs a source outside the code under test, and replaces the oracle with conserved quantities: the shares sum to total_cents, there are exactly `people` shares, and no two shares differ by more than one cent.
expectations: Says the expected side reruns the algorithm under test and cannot catch a mistake both share
Points to testing:test-value for the independent-source rule
Proposes the shares-sum-to-total check or another invariant that does not recompute the split

evals.name: python-repo-loads-only-python-reference
evals.prompt: This repository is Python only: a pyproject.toml and pytest, no package.json and no .csproj. Write a property-based test for normalize_tags, which lowercases, deduplicates and sorts a list of tags.
evals.expected_output: Routes to context/property.md, detects Python as the language of the code under test, and loads only context/property/python.md. Writes properties such as running normalize_tags on its own output changes nothing, and the output is sorted with no duplicates. Does not read the TypeScript or C# references.
expectations: Does not load context/property/typescript.md or context/property/csharp.md
States that a second normalize_tags pass leaves the result unchanged

evals.name: unsupported-language-loads-no-reference
evals.prompt: Our Go module has a Merge function for interval lists that should be commutative. Write a property-based test for it.
evals.expected_output: Routes to context/property.md and uses its language-neutral guidance: commutativity as the invariant, generators that build valid interval lists directly. Loads none of the Python, TypeScript or C# references because the code under test is in none of those languages, and checks which property library the module already uses instead of assuming one.
expectations: States commutativity (merging a with b equals merging b with a) as the property

evals.name: test-passes-when-imports-return-nothing
evals.expected_output: Walks the per-cycle checklist and flags the last item: the test keeps passing even when buildReceipt returns nothing, because it asserts on the order fixture it built, not on the receipt. Proposes asserting the lines of the receipt buildReceipt returns, with expected values taken from the order's stated content.
expectations: States that the test keeps passing when buildReceipt returns nothing
Identifies that the assertion reads the order fixture rather than the receipt
Proposes asserting on the receipt buildReceipt returns
